question: Should memory-core solve this with agents.list[].dreaming overrides, a global plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.agents allowlist, a schedule/stagger option, or a staged combination?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent config location and schedule scope are product/API choices with compatibility impact; two open PRs already explore different implementation shapes.

options.title: Land scoped allowlist or opt-out first
options.body: Accept a small schema-backed scoping control for which agents are swept, then track schedule/stagger behavior separately if still needed.

options.title: Require schedule/stagger in the same feature
options.body: Hold candidate PRs until they also model non-overlapping scheduled runs, at the cost of a larger config and cron design change.

options.title: Use pressure gating instead of new config
options.body: Reject per-agent scoping for now and rely on managed dreaming pressure/backoff work to reduce OOM risk without adding operator config.

recommendation.title: Land scoped allowlist or opt-out first
recommendation.body: Accept a small schema-backed scoping control for which agents are swept, then track schedule/stagger behavior separately if still needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest recent history signal is on the dreaming resolver/runtime path and its managed cron behavior.
